Subject: Post-demo: embedding + reranker integration + repro notes

Thanks again for the quick demo today — appreciated the context on your search+QA pipeline. Recap and immediate next steps from our side:

- Goal: reduce production 5xx incidents when running embeddings -> reranker flow on long documents (~5k tokens).
- What we saw on the call: occasional 5xx from the inference layer when client payloads exceed ~400KB; timeouts around 30s.
- Immediate ask from Orchid: reproducible test case + logs so our infra/serving team can triage.

Can you drop the sample payload and the request logs from your failing run? That’ll let us reproduce locally. I attached a short integration checklist for SDK config (auth, timeout settings, chunking recommendations) — please use if convenient.

Next steps:
1) Lily/platform-ops: send sample request + logs (orchid_embeds.log) — aim for <EOD Mon PT if possible.
2) We’ll reproduce and get back with a suggested temp workaround (client timeout, model variant) and a mitigation plan for Dedicated routing or cache-friendly batch settings.
3) If reproducible, we’ll open an internal ticket and schedule a 60-min debug call with your infra team.

Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf (SDK prefs, timeout examples)

Thanks,
Priyom

Thanks Priyom — attaching the logs and a sample payload we used in prod. The key details:
- Payload is ~475KB after base64 encoding of attachments; we send a single request with embeddings + candidate reranker calls (combined).
- Errors we saw: intermittent 502/503 from the inference endpoint, usually after ~25–35s. We also saw an internal error message: "KV cache allocation failed" in one trace.
- We’re on SDK v0.9.2 (python) and using default client timeout (30s).

Attaching: orchid_embeds.log, sample-payload.json

Appreciate a look — we can make time for a debug call this week.

Subject: Re: Post-demo: embedding + reranker integration + repro notes

Lily — thanks for sending the logs and payload. Quick read and a reproducibility plan from infra/SDK side:

What I see in your log snippets: repeated partial responses from the model host then a 502, plus the "KV cache allocation failed" which indicates the runtime attempted to reserve a large KV cache for long context but ran out on the selected node.

Hypothesis: the combined embeddings + reranker request is causing the runtime to pick a node profile that doesn't have sufficient KV cap for that sequence length and the fallbacks are producing 5xx. Also client timeout of 30s is borderline for the sequence sizes you described.

Repro steps I’ll run here:
- Use your sample-payload.json and send via curl + our python SDK (v0.9.3 internal build).
- Try three routing configs: hosted-default, dedicated-small (lower KV), and dedicated-large (higher KV).
- Run with client timeouts: 30s, 60s, 120s.
- Toggle prefix caching off/on.

Temporary workarounds to try now:
1) Increase client-side timeout to 120s. For python SDK: client = RedwoodClient(timeout=120)
2) Break the large request into two — embeddings first (batch chunk 512 tokens) then reranker over top-N candidates.
3) If using Dedicated, pin to dedicated-large routing profile.

Can you confirm whether you need us to reproduce on your account (we can request temporary access) or if you want to run the curl snippet yourself? If you prefer we run it, please share a short-lived API key or let us run in a replay mode against a sanitized version of the payload.

--Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: platform-ops@orchiddata.com
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:47:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: embedding + reranker integration + repro notes

Marissa — thanks. Some additional details from our infra team:
- We reproduced locally and see 503 when the combined payload includes 6+ attachments and a long prompt (document ~5.4k tokens).
- We currently chunk at 512 tokens, then concatenate embeddings for reranker input. The full encoded payload ends up ~470–500KB.
- We do not use prefix caching intentionally (history gets rebuilt each request).

Attached a sanitized sample-payload.json that fails in our staging. We can create a short-lived API key if you prefer Redwood to run the repro.

Logs excerpt:
> 2027-05-03T15:31:04Z ERROR inference-host-17: response=502, reason=KV cache allocation failed, requested_kv=1.8GB, available=1.6GB
> 2027-05-03T15:31:04Z WARN client: request_duration=34.2s

We’re open to the two-workflow suggestion. The main thing is minimizing changes to our batching logic because it’s baked into our pipeline.

—orchid platform ops
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lily Zhang <lily@orchiddata.com>, platform-ops@orchiddata.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: embedding + reranker integration + repro notes

Thanks all — summary and immediate plan from support/infra: 

1) Repro confirmed (orchid sample payload fails in staging with KV allocation errors). Ticket created: RDINF-1248 (link below).
2) Short-term workaround (we recommend you apply immediately):
   - Increase client timeout to 120s (client side)
   - On Redwood SDK: set routing_preference = "dedicated-large" or use the hosted variant that advertises high-kv-capacity
   - If you must keep single-request flow, reduce per-request context by compressing attachments or moving binary blobs to object storage and passing references.
3) Medium-term: we’ll push a runtime fallback that selects a node with higher KV reservation when combined embeddings+rerkanker sequences are detected, and add safer OOM handling so we return a 429 instead of a 5xx. ETA for a canary patch: 2 weeks.

Can we schedule a 60-min debug session with your infra team tomorrow (Wed) at 10am PT? We’ll bring Marissa and Rishi from infra and I’ll run through the repro live. I’ve attached the support ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RDINF-1248

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
